passages.text: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said: “Who is this who obscures My counsel by words without knowledge?
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD has all power and wisdom.
The LORD spoke to Job.
The LORD spoke from the whirlwind.
The LORD said these words.
The LORD asked a question.
The LORD said, “Who is this?”
The LORD said, “Who darkens My counsel?”
The LORD said, “Who uses words without knowledge?”
passages.original: וַיַּֽעַן־ יְהוָ֣ה אֶת־ אִ֭יּוֹב מִנ הַסְּעָרָה וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ מִ֤י זֶ֨ה׀ מַחְשִׁ֖יךְ עֵצָ֥ה בְמִלִּ֗ין בְּֽלִי־ דָֽעַת׃

passages.text: Now brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform Me.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Job from the whirlwind.
The LORD is powerful and wise.
The LORD said to Job, "Prepare yourself like a man."
Stand firm and be ready.
I, the LORD, will ask you questions.
You must answer Me.
passages.original: אֱזָר־ נָ֣א כְגֶ֣בֶר חֲלָצֶ֑יךָ וְ֝אֶשְׁאָלְךָ֗ וְהוֹדִיעֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Tell Me, if you have understanding.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Job from the whirlwind.
The LORD is all-powerful and wise.
The LORD created the earth.
The LORD said, “Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth?”
The LORD asked Job to answer if he had understanding.
The LORD challenged Job to explain, if he knew.
passages.original: אֵיפֹ֣ה הָ֭יִיתָ בְּיָסְדִי־ אָ֑רֶץ הַ֝גֵּ֗ד אִם־ יָדַ֥עְתָּ בִינָֽה׃

passages.text: Who fixed its measurements? Surely you know! Or who stretched a measuring line across it?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Job.
God asks Job about the earth.
God says, "Who fixed the earth’s measurements?"
God says, "You must know."
God says, "Who stretched a measuring line across the earth?"
passages.original: מִי־ שָׂ֣ם מְ֭מַדֶּיהָ כִּ֣י תֵדָ֑ע א֤וֹ מִֽי־ נָטָ֖ה עָלֶ֣יהָ קָּֽו׃

passages.text: On what were its foundations set, or who laid its cornerstone, while the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Job.
God asked about the creation of the earth.
God asked, “What supported the earth’s foundations?”
God asked, “Who placed the earth’s cornerstone?”
God said the morning stars sang together at creation.
God said all the sons of God shouted for joy at that time.
passages.original: עַל־ מָ֭ה אֲדָנֶ֣יהָ הָטְבָּ֑עוּ א֥וֹ מִֽי־ יָ֝רָ֗ה אֶ֣בֶן פִּנָּתָֽהּ׃ בְּרָן־ יַ֭חַד כּ֣וֹכְבֵי בֹ֑קֶר וַ֝יָּרִ֗יעוּ כָּל־ בְּנֵ֥י אֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: Who enclosed the sea behind doors when it burst forth from the womb, when I made the clouds its garment and thick darkness its blanket, when I fixed its boundaries and set in place its bars and doors, and I declared: ‘You may come this far, but no farther; here your proud waves must stop’?
passages.sermon:
God created the sea.
God enclosed the sea behind doors.
The sea burst forth from the womb.
God made the clouds the sea’s garment.
God made thick darkness the sea’s blanket.
God fixed boundaries for the sea.
God set bars and doors in place for the sea.
God declared to the sea, “You may come this far, but no farther.”
God commanded, “Here your proud waves must stop.”
passages.original: וַיָּ֣סֶךְ בִּדְלָתַ֣יִם יָ֑ם בְּ֝גִיח֗וֹ מֵרֶ֥חֶם יֵצֵֽא׃ בְּשׂוּמִ֣י עָנָ֣ן לְבֻשׁ֑וֹ וַ֝עֲרָפֶ֗ל חֲתֻלָּתֽוֹ׃ וָאֶשְׁבֹּ֣ר עָלָ֣יו חֻקִּ֑י וָֽ֝אָשִׂ֗ים בְּרִ֣יחַ וּדְלָתָֽיִם׃ וָאֹמַ֗ר עַד־ פֹּ֣ה תָ֭בוֹא וְלֹ֣א תֹסִ֑יף וּפֹ֥א־ יָ֝שִׁ֗ית בִּגְא֥וֹן גַּלֶּֽיךָ׃

passages.text: In your days, have you commanded the morning or assigned the dawn its place, that it might spread to the ends of the earth and shake the wicked out of it?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Job.
God asks Job about his power and knowledge.
God says, "Have you ever commanded the morning?"
God asks, "Have you ever told the dawn where to appear?"
God says the morning light spreads to the ends of the earth.
God says the light shakes the wicked out of the earth.
passages.original: הְֽ֭מִיָּמֶיךָ צִוִּ֣יתָ בֹּ֑קֶר יִדַּעְתָּה שַׁחַר מְקֹמֽוֹ׃ לֶ֭אֱחֹז בְּכַנְפ֣וֹת הָאָ֑רֶץ וְיִנָּעֲר֖וּ רְשָׁעִ֣ים מִמֶּֽנָּה׃

passages.text: The earth takes shape like clay under a seal; its hills stand out like the folds of a garment.
passages.sermon:
God shapes the earth.
He forms it like clay pressed by a seal.
The hills rise up on the earth.
They stand out like the folds in a garment.
passages.original: תִּ֭תְהַפֵּךְ כְּחֹ֣מֶר חוֹתָ֑ם וְ֝יִֽתְיַצְּב֗וּ כְּמ֣וֹ לְבֽוּשׁ׃

passages.text: Light is withheld from the wicked, and their upraised arm is broken.
passages.sermon: God withholds light from wicked people.\r\nGod breaks the proud arm of the wicked.
passages.original: וְיִמָּנַ֣ע מֵרְשָׁעִ֣ים אוֹרָ֑ם וּזְר֥וֹעַ רָ֝מָ֗ה תִּשָּׁבֵֽר׃

passages.text: Have you journeyed to the vents of the sea or walked in the trenches of the deep?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Job.
God asks Job questions.
God asks, “Have you gone to the deepest parts of the sea?”
God asks, “Have you walked in the deep places under the water?”
passages.original: הֲ֭בָאתָ עַד־ נִבְכֵי־ יָ֑ם וּבְחֵ֥קֶר תְּ֝ה֗וֹם הִתְהַלָּֽכְתָּ׃

passages.text: Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Have you seen the gates of the shadow of death?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Job.
God asks Job questions.
God asks about death.
God says, "Have you seen the gates of death?"
God says, "Have you seen the gates of the shadow of death?"
passages.original: הֲנִגְל֣וּ לְ֭ךָ שַׁעֲרֵי־ מָ֑וֶת וְשַׁעֲרֵ֖י צַלְמָ֣וֶת תִּרְאֶֽה׃

passages.text: Have you surveyed the extent of the earth? Tell Me, if you know all this.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Job.
God asks Job a question.
God says, "Have you examined the whole earth?"
God says, "Have you seen how wide the earth is?"
God says, "Tell Me, if you know everything about it."
passages.original: הִ֭תְבֹּנַנְתָּ עַד־ רַחֲבֵי־ אָ֑רֶץ הַ֝גֵּ֗ד אִם־ יָדַ֥עְתָּ כֻלָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: Where is the way to the home of light? Do you know where darkness resides, so you can lead it back to its border? Do you know the paths to its home?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Job.
God asks Job about creation.
God asks, "Where is the way to the home of light?"
God asks, "Where does darkness live?"
God asks, "Can you take darkness to its border?"
God asks, "Do you understand the paths to the home of darkness?"
passages.original: אֵי־ זֶ֣ה הַ֭דֶּרֶךְ יִשְׁכָּן־ א֑וֹר וְ֝חֹ֗שֶׁךְ אֵי־ זֶ֥ה מְקֹמֽוֹ׃ כִּ֣י תִ֭קָּחֶנּוּ אֶל־ גְּבוּל֑וֹ וְכִֽי־ תָ֝בִ֗ין נְתִיב֥וֹת בֵּיתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Surely you know, for you were already born! And the number of your days is great!
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Job.
God asks Job if he knows all things.
God says, "You must know, because you were born long ago."
God says, "You have lived many days."
God uses irony to show Job's limited knowledge.
God reminds Job that Job is not eternal or all-knowing.
passages.original: יָ֭דַעְתָּ כִּי־ אָ֣ז תִּוָּלֵ֑ד וּמִסְפַּ֖ר יָמֶ֣יךָ רַבִּֽים׃

passages.text: Have you entered the storehouses of snow or observed the storehouses of hail, which I hold in reserve for times of trouble, for the day of war and battle?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Job.
God asks Job a question.
God says, “Have you entered the storehouses of snow?”
God also says, “Have you seen the storehouses of hail?”
God explains the purpose of these storehouses.
God says, “I keep snow and hail in reserve.”
God says, “I save them for times of trouble.”
God says, “I use them for the day of war and battle.”
passages.original: הֲ֭בָאתָ אֶל־ אֹצְר֣וֹת שָׁ֑לֶג וְאֹצְר֖וֹת בָּרָ֣ד תִּרְאֶֽה׃ אֲשֶׁר־ חָשַׂ֥כְתִּי לְעֶת־ צָ֑ר לְי֥וֹם קְ֝רָ֗ב וּמִלְחָמָֽה׃

passages.text: In which direction is the lightning dispersed, or the east wind scattered over the earth?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Job.
God asks Job about the natural world.
God says, "Where does the light go?"
God asks, "Who sends the lightning in its path?"
God says, "Who scatters the east wind over the earth?"
passages.original: אֵי־ זֶ֣ה הַ֭דֶּרֶךְ יֵחָ֣לֶק א֑וֹר יָפֵ֖ץ קָדִ֣ים עֲלֵי־ אָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: Who cuts a channel for the flood or clears a path for the thunderbolt, to bring rain on a barren land, on a desert where no man lives, to satisfy the parched wasteland and make it sprout with tender grass?
passages.sermon:
God is the Creator.
God has power over nature.
God cuts a channel for the flood.
God clears a path for the thunderbolt.
God brings rain on a barren land.
God sends rain on a desert where no man lives.
God satisfies the parched wasteland.
God makes the wasteland sprout with tender grass.
passages.original: מִֽי־ פִלַּ֣ג לַשֶּׁ֣טֶף תְּעָלָ֑ה וְ֝דֶ֗רֶךְ לַחֲזִ֥יז קֹלֽוֹת׃ לְ֭הַמְטִיר עַל־ אֶ֣רֶץ לֹא־ אִ֑ישׁ מִ֝דְבָּ֗ר לֹא־ אָדָ֥ם בּֽוֹ׃ לְהַשְׂבִּ֣יעַ שֹׁ֭אָה וּמְשֹׁאָ֑ה וּ֝לְהַצְמִ֗יחַ מֹ֣צָא דֶֽשֶׁא׃

passages.text: Does the rain have a father? Who has begotten the drops of dew?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Job.
God asks about the rain and the dew.
God says, “Does the rain have a father?”
God says, “Who gives birth to the drops of dew?”
passages.original: הֲיֵשׁ־ לַמָּטָ֥ר אָ֑ב א֥וֹ מִי־ ה֝וֹלִ֗יד אֶגְלֵי־ טָֽל׃

passages.text: From whose womb does the ice emerge? Who gives birth to the frost from heaven, when the waters become hard as stone and the surface of the deep is frozen?
passages.sermon:
God is the Creator.
God controls nature.
Ice comes from God.
Frost from heaven is born by God.
Water becomes hard like stone because of God.
The surface of the deep freezes because God commands it.
passages.original: מִבֶּ֣טֶן מִ֭י יָצָ֣א הַקָּ֑רַח וּכְפֹ֥ר שָׁ֝מַיִם מִ֣י יְלָדֽוֹ׃ כָּ֭אֶבֶן מַ֣יִם יִתְחַבָּ֑אוּ וּפְנֵ֥י תְ֝ה֗וֹם יִתְלַכָּֽדוּ׃

passages.text: Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades or loosen the belt of Orion?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Job.
God asks Job about the heavens.
God mentions the Pleiades.
The Pleiades are a group of stars.
God asks, "Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades?"
God mentions Orion.
Orion is a constellation.
God asks, "Can you loosen the belt of Orion?"
passages.original: הַֽ֭תְקַשֵּׁר מַעֲדַנּ֣וֹת כִּימָ֑ה אֽוֹ־ מֹשְׁכ֖וֹת כְּסִ֣יל תְּפַתֵּֽחַ׃

passages.text: Can you bring forth the constellations in their seasons or lead out the Bear and her cubs?
passages.sermon:
God created the heavens.
God controls the stars and constellations.
God brings out the constellations at the right time.
God leads the Bear constellation and her cubs.
You cannot bring forth the constellations in their seasons.
You cannot lead out the Bear and her cubs.
passages.original: הֲתֹצִ֣יא מַזָּר֣וֹת בְּעִתּ֑וֹ וְ֝עַ֗יִשׁ עַל־ בָּנֶ֥יהָ תַנְחֵֽם׃

passages.text: Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you set their dominion over the earth?
passages.sermon:
God created the heavens.
God established laws for the heavens.
You do not know these laws.
You cannot set the order of the heavens over the earth.
Only God rules the heavens and the earth.
passages.original: הֲ֭יָדַעְתָּ חֻקּ֣וֹת שָׁמָ֑יִם אִם־ תָּשִׂ֖ים מִשְׁטָר֣וֹ בָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: Can you command the clouds so that a flood of water covers you?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Job.
God asks Job a question.
God is all-powerful.
God controls nature.
God controls the clouds.
God asks, "Can you command the clouds?"
God asks, "Can you make the clouds obey your voice?"
God asks, "Can you cause a flood of water to cover you?"
God shows that only He has this power.
passages.original: הֲתָרִ֣ים לָעָ֣ב קוֹלֶ֑ךָ וְֽשִׁפְעַת־ מַ֥יִם תְּכַסֶּֽךָּ׃

passages.text: Can you send the lightning bolts on their way? Do they report to you, ‘Here we are’?
passages.sermon:
God controls the lightning bolts.
God sends them on their way.
You cannot send lightning bolts.
Lightning bolts do not report to you.
They do not say to you, "Here we are."
passages.original: הַֽתְשַׁלַּ֣ח בְּרָקִ֣ים וְיֵלֵ֑כוּ וְיֹאמְר֖וּ לְךָ֣ הִנֵּֽנוּ׃

passages.text: Who has put wisdom in the heart or given understanding to the mind?
passages.sermon:
God is the Creator.
God gives wisdom to the heart.
God gives understanding to the mind.
No one else can do this.
passages.original: מִי־ שָׁ֭ת בַּטֻּח֣וֹת חָכְמָ֑ה א֤וֹ מִֽי־ נָתַ֖ן לַשֶּׂ֣כְוִי בִינָֽה׃

passages.text: Who has the wisdom to count the clouds? Or who can tilt the water jars of the heavens when the dust hardens into a mass and the clods of earth stick together?
passages.sermon:
God is all-wise and all-powerful.
God alone understands the heavens.
God alone can count the clouds.
God alone can tilt the water jars of the sky.
God acts when the dust becomes hard.
God acts when the clods of earth stick together.
No human can do these things.
Only God has this wisdom and power.
passages.original: מִֽי־ יְסַפֵּ֣ר שְׁחָקִ֣ים בְּחָכְמָ֑ה וְנִבְלֵ֥י שָׁ֝מַ֗יִם מִ֣י יַשְׁכִּֽיב׃ בְּצֶ֣קֶת עָ֭פָר לַמּוּצָ֑ק וּרְגָבִ֥ים יְדֻבָּֽקוּ׃

passages.text: Can you hunt the prey for a lioness or satisfy the hunger of young lions when they crouch in their dens and lie in wait in the thicket?
passages.sermon:
God is the Creator.
God is all-powerful.
God provides for every creature.
You are not able to hunt prey for a lioness.
You cannot satisfy the hunger of young lions.
Young lions crouch in their dens.
They lie in wait in the thicket.
You do not feed them.
God alone provides for them.
passages.original: הֲתָצ֣וּד לְלָבִ֣יא טָ֑רֶף וְחַיַּ֖ת כְּפִירִ֣ים תְּמַלֵּֽא׃ כִּי־ יָשֹׁ֥חוּ בַמְּעוֹנ֑וֹת יֵשְׁב֖וּ בַסֻּכָּ֣ה לְמוֹ־ אָֽרֶב׃

passages.text: Who provides food for the raven when its young cry out to God as they wander about for lack of food?
passages.sermon: God provides food for the raven.\r\nYoung ravens cry out to God.\r\nThey wander because they have no food.
passages.original: מִ֤י יָכִ֥ין לָעֹרֵ֗ב צֵ֫יד֥וֹ כִּֽי־ יְלָדוֹ אֶל־ אֵ֣ל יְשַׁוֵּ֑עוּ יִ֝תְע֗וּ לִבְלִי־ אֹֽכֶל׃
